text:
Maria Vazquez: seeing a spike in GPU task failures across prod-gpu-2 in us-west-2, started ~20m ago. some pods OOM'd then nodes remounted /var/lib/kubelet read-only. nvme errors in dmesg.
Dan Liu: ugh, same cluster. IOPS spiking to ~600k for metadata ops on ephemeral SSDs according to iostat.
Tyler S: any recent batch jobs that churn a lot of small files? that pattern causes metadata storms on thin-provisioned pools.
Maria Vazquez: we rolled out a large retraining job that writes many checkpoints and we run the ephemeral-cleaner to reclaim after pods finish. cleaner runs every 5m and does parallel rm on checkpoints.
Sophia (bot): alert: nvme_smart_threshold_exceeded on node gpu-02a (alert_id: a3f9).
Akshay Patel: can you paste the tail of dmesg and the output of `iostat -xz 1 3` and `lsblk -o NAME,ROTA,RO,TYPE,SIZE,MOUNTPOINT`?
Maria Vazquez: paste logs:
```
[ 1234.567890] nvme nvme0: I/O 12345 QID 0 timeout, aborting command
[ 1234.570123] nvme nvme0: ctrl 0000:03:00.0, keepalive inactive
[ 1235.001234] EXT4-fs warning (device nvme0n1p1): ext4_rename:2689: inode #234567: comm cleaner: directory rename failed, -5
[ 1236.001567] EXT4-fs (nvme0n1p1): Remounting filesystem read-only
```

And iostat snippet:
```
Device            r/s     w/s     rkB/s   wkB/s  rrqm/s  wrqm/s  %util
nvme0n1          1200   5400  102400  512000    0      320     92.1
nvme0n2           260    800   20480   81920    0       12     75.6
```
Dan Liu: %util in the 90s + high w/s and tiny writes -> metadata heavy. thin provisioning + parallel deletes from cleaner = controller garbage collection and wear-leveling spikes.
Tyler S: immediate steps: 1) cordon the affected nodes, 2) stop ephemeral-cleaner on the cluster, 3) reduce cleaner concurrency and switch to a background rate-limited delete.
Akshay Patel: agree. also we should avoid rm -rf on a directory with millions of inodes — prefer `find . -delete -maxdepth` throttled or `rsync --delete` style patterns. we'll need a mitigation script.
Maria Vazquez: cordoned gpu-02a/gpu-02b. stopped cron `ephemeral-cleaner` via deploy rollback.
Sophia (bot): deploy rollback executed by ops-bot at 2024-04-12T18:24:10Z.
Dan Liu: I'm testing a repro on a dev node with fio metadata workload: `fio --name=meta --ioengine=libaio --iodepth=64 --rw=randrw --bs=4k --size=1G --numjobs=16 --name=meta` to simulate. results show latency tail > 300ms under parallel deletes.
Tyler S: long-term we should: 1) add a circuit-breaker in cleaner to back off on nvme %util > 80, 2) move heavy checkpoint churn to pre-attached network storage or S3, 3) change thin pool policy or use larger block sizes where possible.
Akshay Patel: opening infra ticket INFRA-7243 to track fixes and scope cost impact of moving checkpoint traffic to remote storage.
Maria Vazquez: for now I remounted nodes read-only -> remount attempted read-write after controller cool-down and it succeeded on gpu-02b, but gpu-02a needed a reboot.
Dan Liu: note for postmortem — SMART values showed rising erase counts, controller triggered a temporary throttle. likely accelerated wear from churn.
Tyler S: can we throttle ephemeral-cleaner by default in the helm chart? add `--max-concurrency` and `--delete-rate` flags.
Akshay Patel: agreed. I'll add a canary change to reduce concurrency to 2 and add a measured rate limiter, then roll to non-prod first.
Maria Vazquez: thanks, we'll monitor nvme metrics and reopen if it reappears. :thumbsup:
